utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue, good morning to everyone in the courtroom, and especially also those almost invisible outside the courtroom; the technical staff and the interpreters. It's not that I pay attention to the technical staff since we have a technical problem this morning. The Registry has no access at this very moment to some parts of the computer system, so this might cause us to stop whenever we cannot do without any more. But I suggest to you that we just first start. I see Mr. Piletta-Zanin is back in court. Welcome. Mr. Ierace, I would suggest that we do start, and Madam Registrar will inform us when she gets stuck and if we can't proceed any more. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in Witness L. [The witness entered court] 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Mr. L? Yes. Please be seated. Mr. Ierace, when you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I ask that at this stage, we view the electronically joined photograph, which is P3279A. 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if the technical staff could...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please look at the photograph which appears on the screen in front of you, and can you tell me if you recognise the road that appears in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Having regard to the video which was shown yesterday afternoon - for the transcript, that's P3280B - was that the direction in which you were facing when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And also having regard to that video, does that appear to be the view you had when you were looking straight ahead at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the image be moved to the left slowly. Pause there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the right of the road, was there a slope going upwards to another road, that is, to the right of the road on which you were standing when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I'll withdraw that question for the moment. To the left of the road where you were shot, is there a slope downwards and away from the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to move the photograph to the left. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, indeed to the left, was there a small valley?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the photograph. Please pause the photograph at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does the image in front of you now show the road behind you, that is, the road section that was behind you at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that road there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the photograph to the left. Please pause at that point and move the photograph in an upwards direction. Please continue to pan to the left. And please stop at that point now. Thank you. Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown some photographs which are Exhibit P3261. Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, did you make a statement to the -- to an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor at the Tribunal in September last year and indeed sign that statement on the 15th of September last year, that is, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that you made that statement, were you shown a number of photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you have before you five sheets of paper which contain various photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please look at the first sheet, and I think in the top right-hand corner there are some numbers printed in red which read "02110617." Do you see two photographs on that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the top photograph, do you recognise yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that a photograph taken in October of the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you mark in red a circle on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In particular, did you mark a roof under construction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that you were shot, did that roof, that is that semi-constructed roof, exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the -- excuse me, Mr. President. Might I have access to those photographs so that I can cover a reference to the witness's name. Mr. President, I ask that the top photograph on that page which I have identified be placed on the ELMO. I have taken some steps to obscure the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the photograph which appears on the ELMO at the moment, which I identify as photograph marked BR#1A, you seem to be standing in approximately the position where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It appears from the photograph that, immediately above the semi-constructed roof, there are a collection of buildings. Do you know the name of that area, that is, the area where those buildings in the distance are seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it's part of Poljine, Orahov Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the right of that group of buildings and indeed to the right of you as you appear in that photograph, and slightly above, there appear to be another collection of buildings. One can see red roofs and white buildings. Do you know the name of that area where those buildings appear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know the exact name.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now look at the photograph beneath that one on the same page. Does it appear to be a telephoto photograph of the same group of buildings to the right of you in the first photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to those buildings, do you know which side of the confrontation line they were on at the time that you were shot? 50?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the other side. That is to say, opposite our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the buildings that appear above the semi-constructed roof, that is the area you called, I think, Orahov Brijeg, do you know which side of the confrontation line they were on at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go to the next page of photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And Mr. President, I ask that the top photograph be placed on the ELMO. I identify it as being marked BR#2A.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what appears in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There appears to be a road with two cars on it in the middle of the photograph. And to the left of the photograph, the road curves down and around. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: This side road is what we call Stara Cesta, or the "Old Road."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just to be clear on this, I'm not asking you about the road that branches off the main one; I'm asking you about the name of the -- what appears to be the main road, that is, the road that has two cars on it in that photograph. Do you know the name of that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the main road running from Sarajevo to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do you know its name, if it has one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly, but I think it was the M17.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Branching off it is a side road which extends downwards. Do you know the name of that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the road which is called Stara Cesta, meaning "Old Road."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the second photograph - and perhaps that could now be placed on the ELMO - which I identify as being marked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the marking, perhaps could you find another way of indicating what photograph it is. You'll understand why the marking is perhaps not the best way of...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The photograph marked 2B.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see in that photograph what appears to be the same two roads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that you made your statement on the 15th of September last year, did you place a circle in red ink on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please look at that photograph. And do you see on the lower road what appears to be a semi-constructed roof with a red circle around it? Please look at the photograph on the ELMO itself so you can view the original, or at least a better copy. Did you place that circle there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And indeed, does that indicate the same semi-constructed roof that you marked on one of the photographs on the earlier page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please turn to the next photograph, which bears the number in red on the top right-hand corner 0215-1440. And again, I would ask you to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. turn slowly and look at the photograph itself which is placed on the ELMO to your right. Does this appear to be another photograph of the same two roads but from a different angle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the hill to the top left, there appears to be a tower. What is the name of that hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please turn to the next photograph which bears the numbers in the top right-hand corner 0215-1441. Does that appear to be a larger print of one of the earlier photographs that you have just identified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And finally, turn to the last page, which has in the top right-hand corner the numbers 0215-1442. Does that appear to be a larger print of the first photograph that you looked at and identified? And perhaps that may not be placed on the ELMO at this stage.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you could direct that that not be placed on the ELMO. Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, earlier you said that the two settlements or collections of buildings, you're on their side. Which side was that? Which army was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army that held the whole city under blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb army, the former JNA, parts of it, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness? Mr. L, you'll now be examined --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. L, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, whether you gave statements to the investigators of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before coming to testify, did you talk to the investigators of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that it was the 31st of August, 2000, would you agree with me that that is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember exactly when that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, the Defence would like to show the statement of the 31st of August to the witness for him to identify the signature, to tell us whether it is indeed his signature and his statement, and may we block out the signature? I'd just like the witness to assert whether it is his statement or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest, Ms. Pilipovic, that since I do not expect this to be tendered into evidence as such, but if you just show it to the witness and if you then please indicate for the record what exactly you're showing, and you'll then give an opportunity to the Prosecution to see whether this is the document, as far as I understand, provided by the Prosecution to you. So if you please would indicate what you're showing him. I assume it's a statement of a certain date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence is going to show Witness L the 31st of August, 2000 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the lower half of the statement, there appears a signature. I should -- and on the last page as well. Could the witness tell us whether it is his signature and whether he did indeed give a statement to the investigators on the 31st of August, 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, Mr. Usher, could you just show it to, give it to the witness. Does the Prosecution want to verify whether -- yes. It should not be put on the ELMO. Just show it to the witness, please. And also his signature also on the last page. The signatures, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 39228. So not the last one but the one before last.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: 3228, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see you're nodding but could you please say aloud your answer. Are these your signatures, as you have been asked by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are my signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution want to verify whether this statement is -- Mr. Usher, would you then please show the document just shown to the witness to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, after the witness has identified it, the Defence should like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not think that the content of the document at this moment is at stake, so we'll consider that during the first break, whether it would be proper not to have it tendered into evidence and once the Prosecution also has had an opportunity to state his position. Would you then, since it has just been shown for identification to the witness, would you please give the copy back to Ms. Pilipovic so that she can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness L, yesterday during the examination-in-chief, you said that in October 1993 you were a member of the Civil Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if, as a member of the Civil Defence, what was your role in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically my role was to distribute humanitarian aid to the population in my area, to look after the cleanliness of streets and the whole neighbourhood, and that would roughly be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in relation to the city of Sarajevo, which area was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's "centar," the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This part of the city that you've just mentioned, when you showed them on these photographs, is -- are those photographs showing that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You mean that October, on the 7th October 1993, you were -- were not in that area as a member of the Civil Defence, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the Civil Defence, but I -- but that particular day I was not engaged in the usual chores.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us: Before October 1993, were you also, that is, I mean, 1993 and 1992, were you a member of the Civil Defence then or, rather, when did you join the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined the Civil Defence, I think, in June 1993. So it's June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And before that? Did you play any role, or what did you do prior to June 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And as a member of the Territorial Defence, in which area were you active; in this area or some other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in this area. In the -- in my neighbourhood, in the area where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the Territorial Defence, did you have some ID card or a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the uniform wasn't really much. Whatever one had, one wore. As for some ID card, I didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the Territorial Defence, were you issued with a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not officially because there were no weapons, but we managed as far as weapons were concerned. 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the Civil Defence, did you wear a uniform then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness photograph 0215-1440.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have in front of you photograph 1440. Is that the part of the town in which you were on the 7th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us on this photograph where is it that you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean where I was when I was wounded?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can show it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like -- except that we have a technical problem; I don't know what to do. We would like the witness to mark the place where he was wounded on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, we have -- the witness has told the Court, I think on several occasions, where he was. What's the exact relevance of have him indicate again the place where he was, since -- is there any specific reason why? I mean, we went through the geography of the road I think twice or three times. But if there's any --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence wants the place where the witness was marked because in this -- this photograph best shows the predominating features. The witness has identified the hill. And the next question of the Defence would be after the witness identified the place from -- so my next question would be from which direction did the bullet come?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the problem is, as you'll understand, Ms. Pilipovic, I explained to you yesterday that this is a pre-marked photograph. I just wonder whether we could use it again for marking at trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may assist, this is, in fact, a photograph which has not been marked previously by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're right. I'm mistaken. The others are. So if a black marker would be used, then it could be done. I apologise for my hesitations. Mr. Usher, could you please give a black marker to the witness. And I think it could be put on the ELMO at this stage since there's no -- nothing in the photograph. Would you please put it on the ELMO first, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will mark here the road on which I was at the time of wounding. Now, whether that is the exact spot where I was wounded, I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you at the same time indicate the direction from which the bullet came on this photograph, that is, the spot where you were and from which direction the bullet came.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interests of clarity, I would ask that my friend indicate the manner in which she wants the witness to indicate the direction from which the bullet came. Does she mean by an arrow or something else? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, I have an additional question, Ms. Pilipovic. A photograph is a two-dimensional picture, and this might cause some problems since there's no depth. At least, if there's any depth in the photograph, it's very difficult if you use arrows to indicate depth as well. So would you please, in guiding the witness, tell him exactly how to do it, and also -- well, at least -- I wouldn't say confront him with this problem, but at least make sure that no mistakes will be the result of this difference between two dimensions and three dimensions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, will you please make a small circle to indicate the place where you were at the moment of wounding.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will, but I repeat I can mark the road that I was walking on. Whether I will pinpoint the right place, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as your memory serves you in regard to this road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to the relay on the hill, if we look at this photograph, and it is in the -- it is to the north. If we look at the photograph like this, perhaps northwest, north-northwest. Can you tell us from which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My friend is giving evidence from the bar table, and I suspect the evidence, in fact, is incorrect. I don't know that the hill which contains the relay is to the northwest. I have provided my friend with a map of this area. And I think if she consults that, she will see that, in fact, the hill is to the southeast, as I recollect it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence does not have that photograph, but I will rephrase my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- so as not to waste time on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in relation to this mosque, from which direction did a bullet come?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interests of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to the question. The mosque may or -- I don't want to trespass on my friend's area but if I can point out my objection this way: The mosque may or may not have anything to do with the direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you show us on this photograph, since you were coming down this road -- or were you coming down this road? Or were you going up this road, up the hill, as you told us that it was at the foot of this hill? Will you tell us whether you were climbing down or climbing up this road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was climbing down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, on various photos, the witness has already indicated that he was walking downwards on the small road. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. He did, but the Defence wants to check whether he was going down the road or up the road on this photograph, and that was my only question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you make an arrow to show us which direction did the bullet come.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except that naturally you look upward, up, then it came from the hill. That is where the bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But that is the photograph 1442. And in this photograph 1440, can you show us in this photograph? Because you said you had gone to get bread for your parents, in what direction is your parents' house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that I had gone to buy bread for my parents but that I was carrying, taking bread to my parents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, Defence counsel would like to know whether from the position on the road you indicated several times on photographs whether you went in the direction of the house with the roof under construction, which is downwards, or that you went the other way, upwards, moving away from the house with the unfinished roof. Could you please indicate which direction you went at the time that you were shot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was moving downwards, towards the house that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I hope this assists you, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And in that area that you were in, is there a bakery there or a shop selling bread?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And were you going in this direction? Where it -- was it that you were coming to this area to buy bread for your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I took the bread in my place of residence, that is, in my neighbourhood, and took it along.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you took this road to go your parents' house, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark -- in this area where one can see houses, can you tell us if you -- your parents' house is there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, since there are protective measures, I wonder whether you could get the same information in a different way so that the protective measures would still be effective.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we can remove the photograph and have only the witness marking his parents' house without showing it on the ELMO, and we would then submit this document to the registry to have it sealed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can one see your parents' house on this photograph at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even if procedure --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is my only question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, even that question, since there are -- well, there are some houses but not too many on the picture. Perhaps if it would assist you if I suggest to you that you ask the witness whether the -- that if the house of his parents is on the picture he would then mark it with a circle and letter "P," and if we then show the picture to the Prosecution and to the Bench, and you verify for yourself whether anything was marked on the picture, so that every party is aware of what the witness did and at the same time the protective measures are still fully effective. Would that be a suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. And I did ask the witness to tell us if his parents' house was there. If not, there is no need for him to mark it at all or to mark it as you have suggested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, then, the question is that if the house of your parents is on this photograph, you mark it with a circle and put the letter "P" on it. If the house of your parents is not on the photograph, then of course you'll mark nothing at all. Will you please do that without the photograph being put on the ELMO? You don't have to indicate whether you mark anything or not, just do it if you're able to do it and then the photograph will be given to the usher. So, Mr. Usher, would you then please take the photograph, yes, and show it to the parties so that they can see whether there's any marking with a "P" on it. Now please show it to the Prosecution. Now give it to Madam Registrar. Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, that morning -- you were not going to see your parents that morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was going to my parents, and I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown the photograph 1442.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph, you show the place where you were wounded. Can you tell us what weapon was it that wounded you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the so-called Death Sower.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you say where was -- did that sower -- how far away from you was it, whether in metres or kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know exactly, but it had to be a few hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And on this photograph, could you identify the place where this Death Sower was, those few hundred metres away from you? Can you show it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a few hundred metres. Well, it was ahead of me, somewhere in front of me that the Death Sower was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you identify the place on this photograph? Can you identify the place of where this Death Sower was, the direction from which it came and from which direction the bullet came, according to you. Can one see it on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question. The question presumes that the witness has given evidence that he knows precisely where the weapon was at the time that he was shot. My reading of his answers so far is that he has not done that. And therefore, the question cannot be complied with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. The witness has testified, "I wouldn't know exactly, but it had to be a few hundred metres." And apart from that, the question, Ms. Pilipovic, asks both for a place and a direction, which, of course, is not similar. One has got to do with the other, but you have to ask him either whether he knows the place or he could give a more exact place or a more exact direction or a direction from which the bullet has come.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know the location where the Sower of Death was positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the location, but I know the direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be possible for you to mark on this photograph what direction you're talking about, either with a circle or an arrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There is already before the Trial Chamber abundant evidence as to the direction that the witness heard the shot come from, both in video form and in photograph form, being the very photograph before the Trial Chamber at the moment. If the witness is to be requested Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to mark this photograph to clarify that, then the witness should be given the opportunity to indicate a scope of direction rather than one narrow line or arrow. It should be made clear to him if he doesn't know precisely what line that sound came from, then he should be given the necessary freedom to mark the ambit possibility. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness has testified until now approximately the direction the shot came from, although I do not recollect him saying that he identified this direction from the sound, as your objection seems to suggest. I would allow, nevertheless, Ms. Pilipovic to ask whether he could tell in more detail what direction the bullet came from. So please proceed. The objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph, could you please mark for us the direction, to the best of your recollection, from which the bullet came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Defence please be given the photograph since we cannot see the direction on the screen, the direction which has been marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the problems is that the witness marked partially on the tape covering the head. But I think the two arrows remaining might be clear enough to... Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in response from my learned colleague, you told us about these houses in relation to the confrontation line. I should like to know how far the confrontation line was from where you were standing, from this particular location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the spot where you were standing, do you know where the confrontation lines were of our side, as you refer to it, and Serb lines? Could this be seen on 1442? Again, in relation to the spot where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know where exactly the lines were positioned and whether they could be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So as far as the location where you were is concerned, you don't know where the confrontation lines were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know that -- I know that they were ahead of me. That I know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the confrontation line on your side, as you call it, was? That is, your side of the confrontation line and how far it was from the location where you were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where it was, but I am, of course, sure that the location where I was was on our side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So the confrontation line, that is, your side of the confrontation line, was in front of you, ahead of you? You know that for sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were ahead of me. The part that is closer to where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the area that was closer to you, were there any soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. There were soldiers; however, at that time, I didn't see anyone when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that in the area which could be seen from the location where you were, there was fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. I ask my friend indicate at what stage? Does she mean at the time that he was shot, earlier or later that day, or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please specify, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm referring to 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand it. Your question was about at least approximately the time the witness was shot. I think that's also the relevance of your question. Could you please be more specific as to that day or these days when this event occurred?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: At the time you were wounded, Witness, that is a week before that, was there any conflict, any fighting in the area which you have described, in the area which you have shown as being the area from which the bullet came at the time you were wounded? Was there any fighting going on at that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for sure. However, on the day when I was wounded, I know that there was no fighting. But shooting was relatively frequent and almost exclusively at civilians in the area where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often would you visit this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended. When I had time, I -- I went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And how often did you pass this road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when I went to see my parents.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said the incident took place early in the morning. Did you go to see your parents the day before? I mean, did you spend the night of the 6th -- between the 6th and the 7th at your parents' house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I was not there the day before nor did I spend the night in my parents' house, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That day and that particular night, were you at all in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I was there on the 7th of October, 1993, in early morning hours when I was wounded and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, when you say that there was no fighting on the 7th, in the morning of the 7th, you're referring to that particular morning, the night before, and the day before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day before I went there, my father had come to see me. So I am quite positive that there was no fighting. But of course there was shooting, as he told me, going on from time to time, and he advised me to -- to come to see them before dawn, but that day I was a bit late and it was already light.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So when you say that there was no shooting on that particular day, you actually don't have any personal knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I'm saying is that there was no fighting. But the shooting, on the other hand, was a constant occurrence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On photograph number 1440, in response from my learned colleague, you indicated the Hum hill. Looking at the photograph number 1442, would Hum be behind you, behind your back, or on your side? By using this photograph 1442, would it be possible for you to tell us where the hill, the Hum hill, is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in any case, it would be behind my back or perhaps on my side. I don't know exactly, but it would be behind me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge, either personal knowledge or from your father, that there was a confrontation line on this part of the hill? Was there a confrontation line on this hill?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. I ask my friend indicate clearly what hill she has in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please be more specific, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I refer to the Hum hill. I should like the witness to be shown 1440. I mean, the witness has identified the hill where the TV relay is in response to a question of my colleague. Let me try to be even more specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The hill where the TV relay is situated, is that the Hum hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have the photograph, but yes, yes, that is the hill in question, Hum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the photograph please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, this is Hum.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you described the location where you were on 1442 and when I asked you about a hill that was behind you, were you talking about the Hum hill? Was that the hill that you said was behind your back in relation to this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So my question was: Did you have any personal knowledge or did you happen to learn that from your father where in relation to this hill the confrontation line was? 50?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that for sure. He may have told me that, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any troops below this hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you don't want to tell us the truth, therefore.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, the whole area was full of troops. Whether there were any soldiers below the Hum hill, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that the area was full of troops, would you agree with me, then, that there was fighting going on in this area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President, and ask the witness [sic] to clarify at what stage. I have a second basis for objection; that is relevance. I note the witness has now gone some nine minutes beyond the examination-in-chief time. Whilst I don't have a problem with that per se, there is this I think more fundamental issue of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's not mix up the time issue, which was in my mind as well, and the relevance issue. Ms. Pilipovic, could you explain the relevance of this question where I think a distinction might be made between the presence of troops and actual fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the presence of the troops is relevant for the purposes of testing the credibility of the witness. And since I have gone some nine minutes beyond the examination-in-chief, and in view of the fact that this witness is very important for the Defence, I should like to ask the Court to allow me two more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course you get the opportunity to put two more questions. But do I understand that you're going to rephrase them? Because you said the presence of the troops is of importance for the credibility, but your question was about actual fighting after the witness had already testified about the presence of troops. That was your next question, I think, especially which the objection was against.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us about the presence of troops in this area and in this particular location as well. Do you have any knowledge whether those troops participated in the fighting there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then please specify exactly as far as the moment, day, hour, week, month, whatever you want to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any personal knowledge or any information from your father that in this particular area, in 1993, due to the presence of soldiers, that there was any fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, when you say "in 1993," you are talking about a very long period of time. There was fighting, I am sure. However, at the moment when I was wounded, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us whether you have reported this incident to anyone else except to the medical institution where you went? And when I say "anyone else," I am referring to some competent authorities. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Everything happened very fast. It was only later that my superiors from the Civil Defence organisation learned about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if there was any report made following this incident, and do you know whether any competent authority actually went to the scene of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the area where you visited when you went to see your parents, was there a police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been, but I'm not sure. I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if a Lejla checkpoint was located in the vicinity of the road that you took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have a document that we were given from the OTP. It's an official note made by the Public Security Station officials who visited the scene of the incident and made a note thereof. The note contains a description of the location where Witness L was at the moment he was wounded. We have a sufficient number of copies of this official note, both in English and B/C/S, and I should like the witness to be shown this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Usher, could you please. While the documents are distributed, Ms. Pilipovic, you indicated that you had two more questions five, six minutes ago. May I assume that this is the final part of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I will wind up, Your Honour. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll not have the break at exactly 10.30 but just after you finish this part of the cross-examination. In order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, I see that the note is pre-numbered D29, which I think, Madam Registrar, should be changed since we're already at, I think, D31. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next number is D31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness L, do you have a document titled "Official Note" in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is the document dated 8th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it made by the Vogosca Public Security Station? Can you see that in the upper left corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of this official note, does it say that it was "compiled in the premises of" and so on and so forth? Is that the beginning of the first paragraph of the official note?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does the second paragraph begin with the words: "On the 7th of October, 1993, at 6.30, in the vicinity of the Lejla checkpoint, a citizen" so-and-so "was wounded. Occupation, member of the Civil Defence"?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to notice that the translation only covers part of the statement, then that's what I noticed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the translation ends somewhere in the middle of the document you gave to us. It's -- I think the last line ends with "Kosevsko 1CZ," and that happens to be approximately in the middle of the original in B/C/S. So if you want to question the witness on the document...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have the continuation of the translation, which also contains the medical report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you then please distribute the ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies, but we have only four copies of this particular page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then, since the translation is not of major importance for the witness, would you give, for the time being, one copy to the Prosecution and two ... Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have two more copies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we have the whole translation now, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness L, was there a checkpoint belonging to the Vogosca Public Security Station in the area where you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know that. 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Public Security Station is located in the vicinity of the area where you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether the information contained in this official note is accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. It's fair to the witness to put the particular propositions contained in that note one at a time to the witness rather than to broadly say to the witness words to the effect, "Could you tell us whether the information is accurate?" in other words, all of the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the objection is sustained. Ms. Pilipovic, may I just explain to you that the witness just testified that he didn't know about a checkpoint, and for example, the vicinity of the checkpoint is part of this document. So if there's any specific point you'd like to check, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question was whether the checkpoint Lejla was situated there, and the witness said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to that, Mr. President. That wasn't the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness L, do you know whether there was a Lejla checkpoint in the vicinity of the area where you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I want you to be more precise on these kind of issues. Let me just check exactly what your question was and what the answer was. Your question has been: "Witness L, was there a checkpoint belonging to the Vogosca Public Security Station in the area where you were wounded?" The answer was, "I really don't know that." So that's really something different from what you just told me because that reads: "Your Honour, my question was whether the checkpoint Lejla was situated there, and the witness said no." The answer [sic] was whether there was any checkpoint or not, and he said, "I do not know." So there was no question of a specific checkpoint mentioned and that he said it was not there, which suggests that he had knowledge about where it might have been or at least that it was not in that vicinity. So would you please be more precise on these issues. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness L, do you know whether in the month of October 1993, in the vicinity of the spot where you were wounded was a checkpoint called Lejla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This concludes my cross-examination of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll adjourn until 5 minutes past 11.00. And then, if there's any need, there will be a possibility for re-examination and for, if needed also, questions from the Bench. Until 5 minutes past 11.00, we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Defence has indicated that it intends to tender the statement of the witness which is dated the 31st of August, 2000. As you, Mr. President and Your Honours, would be aware, I have consistently opposed the tender of statements where the -- where it contains material which has not been put to the witness, but on this particular occasion, I do not oppose the tender of the statement. I would like that issue clarified before I commence my re-examination, because the content of that depends to some extent upon your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for giving me the floor. There is a point that I should like to examine. I am rather afraid as to the procedure and its evolvement. There is a point which is not of interest to the witness but is of interest to myself, and I cannot tolerate certain things in this court, as in any other instance or circumstances, and I would prefer it if the witness were to be escorted out of the courtroom so that I could say what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is it an issue which should be raised before the re-examination of the witness starts? I mean, is it of any direct relevance for the re-examination? If not, I'd rather wait until the examination of the witness is finished. But if you say no, it's relevant at this moment, I'll follow your suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence can show itself to be very patient, and we can wait, of course, to see the end of the re-examination of this witness and then to say what we have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll then give you the opportunity to raise the issue you want to raise. So first we have to decide on the tendering into evidence of the statement of the witness, the previous statement given to the investigators. Ms. Pilipovic, we changed the procedure in some -- to some extent by -- since you have shown the paper to the witness, he identified his signature on it and -- do you still would like to tender the statement into evidence, although it has not been, as far as the content is concerned, been touched upon during the examination -- during cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Defence would like to tender the statement into evidence as a Defence exhibit because, from the contents of the statement identified by the witness, and he said that it is indeed his statement and his signature, this brings the credibility of the witness into question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you may have noticed, this Chamber applies as a rule that previous statements are not, at least not as a whole, admitted Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. into evidence. Ms. Pilipovic, since only the signature issue has been part of your cross-examination and since you have not confronted the witness with any specific line, as you could have done, of his previous statement, I'd rather this Chamber finally will decide at the end, as we always do, but is very much not inclined to admit this document into evidence. And since I have heard from the Prosecution the reason why they do not oppose, I suggest that in a similar way as the Defence often has done, by just reading a line to a witness if you want to confront him in one way or another with his previous statement or have it confirmed might be a suitable technique. So then we would not have to change the general line set out by this Chamber not to admit previous statements into evidence unless there is a specific reason for that. So unless -- Mr. Ierace, of course you're perfectly entitled to seek the admission of the statement into evidence by yourself if there's any need for that and if you give proper reasons for that, but -- so you have to expect that the request, the application, the tendering into evidence of this statement by the -- by the Defence will be denied. 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That being the case, I think a safer course is for me to seek leave to ask one further question which really is in the nature of examination-in-chief. And of course, I don't oppose any application by my friend to ask further questions in relation to any answer that might be given in response. And secondly, in due course, I will seek to tender the medical report. I wish to ask one or two questions of the witness by way of identification of that report; likewise, I would have no objection should my friends make an application to ask further questions in relation to that. I identify those two issues, Mr. President. Beyond that, I have a few questions that do fall under the heading of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, am I correct that, until now, the medical report only showed up as part of a translation, and I haven't seen any -- not seen any original? What's the reason why this report would only now be tendered into evidence, which is rather late?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's something that I should have taken the witness to in chief, and that's why I identified it as something that is relevant to evidence-in-chief. And I can indicate that the question, quite separate from that that I seek to ask, goes to the clothing that the witness was wearing at the time he was shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. And of course, Ms. Pilipovic, you will get a fair opportunity to put any additional questions if the re-examination would demand so. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, what were you wearing at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wearing a multicoloured jumper. I had a pair of jeans and track shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P1712. I might indicate, Mr. President, that during the course of cross-examination, I had a clean copy of that exhibit prepared. I think the Registry has that clean copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the document which is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is called a "Traumatological Findings" from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you first see that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I was reading at that moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I am quite sure of what I can see, but could Mr. Ierace please provide me with a copy of the French and English translations of that document. Thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do see that there's an English translation attached to it which bears the number P1712.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reason why I couldn't see you standing up is that I was going through the document. Perhaps if you would do that also next time. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, I'll repeat my question: When did you first see that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said for the first time?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the document first when I was given medical assistance, and they provided me with these findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you receive that medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Kosevo Hospital. And afterwards, after I had been given medical assistance, I was given this piece of paper, these findings. So my answer is: In hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked questions by the Defence as to the direction of the bullet that hit you. You marked on a photograph some arrows in relation to those questions. How were you able to determine the direction from which the bullet came that hit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it. Before the bullet actually struck me, I heard the firing beforehand. There was a short burst of gunfire, two or three bullets were fired, and the bullets whizzed past, either past me or up above my head. And then the second burst of gunfire hit me, one of the bullets from that burst hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In placing the arrows, the two black arrows on the photograph, did you mean to indicate precisely the direction of the bullet or generally the direction of the bullet, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to indicate the direction, the direction from which the bullet came.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate that. I am interested in clarifying the degree of precision that you meant to convey by those two arrows. If I could ask you this way: You have been asked questions about two groups of buildings which were in front of you in the distance. I think you identified one of those groups of buildings as being in the area of Poljine, and you were also asked questions about the group of buildings that appeared above the semi-constructed building -- semi-constructed roof, rather, on photograph 1A of Exhibit P3261.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but could Mr. Ierace indicate precisely where we see that in the transcript, and the Chamber asks for that from time to time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber prefers literal quotation and usually allows a quotation where there is no doubt as to the reliability. But since objection has been raised, could you please find the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are labouring under a difficulty with our LiveNote, but I think I can approach it in a different way. I ask the witness be shown photograph which is part of P3261 and which contains the numbers, in the top right-hand corner, 1442. Perhaps I could see that photograph first, if that's convenient. I would ask that the photograph be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To assist you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, since the Prosecution has some problems, it is at 9.14 and 9.15 where you will find the exact source.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I found it in the interval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- of course, there must be no doubt. If there is any reason to believe that the quotation is not correct, it certainly should be more precise, a literal quotation. That's what we always ask for. But the mere fact that there has been a frequent question to quote literally because there is some doubt as to the correctness of the quotation, whether the doubt is justified or not, is a second issue, but times it does not come into our minds immediately what has been said before. On the other hand, I'd like to prevent very often this Chamber and the other parties, the parties, both parties, often accept a quotation if it is in conformity with their recollection. So whenever you ask for literal quotation, I would say the mere fact that it has been asked at other occasions is not a very satisfying ground for asking it. I think there should always be some concern about the correctness of the quotation. So if you could keep that in mind, because we are not on the playground, we are in a serious court of law. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, I think a few moments ago you said that you determined the direction from the sound of the shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would like to clarify with you the extent that you were able to determine the direction, having regard to the sound, in relation to the two arrows that you have placed on the photograph which is now on the ELMO. Could you assist us with what you meant to convey with those arrows? In other words, do you say that you could determine that the bullet came from either of those two directions indicated by the arrows or somewhere in the space between the arrows or somewhere in that general direction, that is, encompassing an area either side of the two arrows? Can you assist us in that regard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside the space between the two arrows, that would be more or less it. So the space between the two arrows. That's what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recollect whether, at the time, you noticed if there were any dwellings or other human construction in the area between the two arrows on the photograph, that is, at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic, we have only additional questions, of course, limited to the issue just covered by -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you said that after you were wounded, you were taken to hospital, to Kosevo hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but before that, I was given first aid in the local infirmary, if I can call it that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where is that local infirmary? Where is it located in respect to the spot you were wounded at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Going towards town, towards the centre of town, about 500 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have in your possession the original of the document that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. my learned colleague showed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence objects to this medical document because it has not been signed by the authorised physician, and it is illegible as well. So we question the credibility and challenge the credibility of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll give a decision on that. So it's about the lack of the signature and the illegibility which is the basis for the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from my colleagues? A question or more questions will now be put to you by Judge El Mahdi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like you to tell me, please, the direction of the bullet that hit you in the arm. You said that it was next to the shoulder, that you were hit near the shoulder, wounded near the shoulder. But what direction, from top to bottom or vice versa? Let me explain my question. In the report, it says, or rather, it describes that there were two holes without specifying the direction that the bullet took. So could you enlighten us on that point, please? Could you explain to us how you were actually hit. 50?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance wound, the bullet pierced the arm a little higher up. The entrance wound was higher than the exit wound, so it would be logical to suppose that it had been fired from an altitude because the bullet went from a higher point and exited at a lower point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but was it your left arm? If I understood you correctly, your left arm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my left upper arm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the area you indicated that the shot had come from, I thought it was to your right. Was it slightly to your right from the point you were standing at? Judging from the photograph, I would say it was to your right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was frontal, straight ahead, a frontal hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the bullet hit you inside -- on one side, if I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The bullet entered here and exited on the back side of my arm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And one last question: You said that you sought shelter, cover, in a canal, in a sort of ravine. Where was that located with respect to the road you were on when you were hit? You said you took cover somewhere. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a canal or a ditch right by the road, drain. And it was about -- it was less than a metre deep, this canal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we can't see the canal on the photograph. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably not because of the greenery and growth and grass, but it is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was it to the right of the road or to the left of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was to my right. So at the moment I was hit, this canal was to my right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what about the car that came a little later to save you and take you to hospital? Where did the car come from? What direction was the car coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: The car was coming along the road that I, myself, was moving along. So it was moving towards my parents' place, the same direction as myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was the car also targeted? Did they shoot at the car, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have also one question for you. You told the Court that you saw the medical document for the first time in the hospital. Was this document given to you by the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They gave it to me in the hospital.
