utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you go back to the hospital at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, for the checkup.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you then take the document with you to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there then an additional entry on the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes, I believe so. I think it is recorded in the finding that the examination was performed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was then the document returned to you again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the document you had then in your possession, did you give that very document to the investigators, or was there any photocopy made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember, but I have the original document so that I suppose I gave the original to them and then they copied it. I'm not quite sure. But I was returned the original, and I'm in the possession of the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you bring the original with you today, or is it still in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not bring it here. It is in Sarajevo. I just brought a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have to decide on the documents tendered into evidence, but I'd like first to confer shortly with my colleagues. [Trial Chamber confers] 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So let's now proceed to the admission into evidence of the several documents. Madam Registrar, would you please assist me. But as far as my recollection goes, we start with P3280B, if I'm correct. That's a video, similar video as shown in other witnesses at other occasions. Since there's no objections, it's admitted into evidence. Then we have the -- yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence objected to the video yesterday, and we said that this tape was not complete. And for reasons when we objected to the video material shown to Witness L, and we objected -- I said -- excuse me, I said Witness L but I meant Witness G. So this videotape is not complete. Only the scene on the incident was recorded but not the place about which Witness L claims that a bullet was fired from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are saying that a similar objection you made yesterday in respect of Witness G, you'd like to make on Witness L. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is right, Your Honour. That is right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday, a decision has been given as far as Witness G is concerned, and it has been explained to you that the completeness as such, whether there could have been more information on a video, is not a matter of admissibility. And of course, the Defence is entirely free to tender into evidence whatever videos on other locations related to the incident. But the decision, therefore, is the same as it was yesterday in respect of the video used for Witness G. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have the 360-degree photograph. That's P3279A, as far as my recollection goes. Since there's no objection, it's admitted into evidence. And we have P3261, which is five sheets of photographs appearing seven photographs on these five sheets, the first two pages bearing two photographs, with the special annotation that the exhibit as tendered, after marking by the -- by the witness on the request of the Defence, includes a tiny little yellow piece of paper with part of the markings on it, on the photograph, with number 12151442. So that yellow piece of paper and the markings on it is part of the evidence. Then we have P1712, a medical report, and attached to it -- and translation to English 1712.1, English translation of the same medical report. Objections have been made to the admission into evidence on two grounds, the first ground being that they are not signed. First of all, the Chamber sees that wherever there is a stamp on the document, it -- usually there is some kind of a handwritten text which we assume is the -- a signature of the one who is responsible for the text above it and who had access to the stamp. So it seems that there is -- the first objection is without grounds, at least on the copy as we have it here. The second issue raised was the illegibility. The mere fact that part of a document is in handwriting as such that you can't read it is not a matter of admissibility since the Defence, if there's any need to rely upon the illegible part of the document, of course could call whatever witness and see whether any explanation could be given for that. At this moment, of course, the probative value is restricted to those parts visible, and the Court is aware that parts of the text cannot be read at this moment, which asks for great caution in assessing the probative value of the document. So therefore, Exhibit P1712 is admitted into evidence, and 1712.1 as well. But it should be under seal because the name of the witness appears on it. Similarly, since the name of the witness also appears on the set of seven photos on five sheets, that should be under seal as well. And then Madam Registrar reminds me that -- yes. There's still the -- yes. We -- I did make a mistake -- no. I've forgotten one document. That's Defence document which is pre-numbered D31, which is the report on an incident, and D31.1 is the English translation of that document. But, Madam Registrar, I think we have a small problem here. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We had a small -- we had a small problem since D31.2 -- D31.1 was not complete. Did you meanwhile find it, Madam Registrar? You have a complete translation now. So these two documents will be admitted as Defence Exhibits D31 and D31.1. I think we went through all the paperwork then. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. It is simply for the transcript, for the sake of precision. The Defence believes that on page 47, line 19, 0010 -- 14151241 [as interpreted] is the English transcript. This is merely the formal matter, the matter of that transcript, but I think it needs to be said that it is the transcript Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in the English language, just for the sake of precision. Have you found all these references?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... line. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The numbers which I see on the exhibits is not 12 but 012, unless you have a different exhibit before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- could you please explain, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? I've got in front of me now page 47, line 19, which reads in the English transcript "... on the photograph, with number 12151442."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is 01, zero one. Or am I wrong? The reference that I have is there is a zero.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And one needs to be as precise as possible so that we are sure that we have the same document before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. It is actually 0215 and then 1442. Thank you for your assistance. So we have done all of that. Then, Mr. L, this is the end of your examination by the parties and by this Bench. You understand that we are dependent on information given to us by those who come and testify in this court, and documents, for the decisions we'll have to take. We thank you very much for having come this long way, and I hope that you'll come home safely. Mr. Usher, would you then -- unless there's any reason at this moment, Ms. Pilipovic, not to have the witness led out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The question -- my question has to do with the admission of documents. Perhaps I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... it's about the admission of the documents tendered in relation to this witness? [The witness withdrew] 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is right, in relation to the photographs. Perhaps I didn't understand. This is the photograph which was also marked by this witness. 1440 on which he also drew --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the specific remark I made was that the marking on the photograph 0215-1442 was a marking which did not just touch the photo itself but also the yellow small sticker on it. So that should remain part of the exhibit as well. That's the reason why I made specific mention of that issue. But of course the photos are admitted into evidence as marked by the witness. Does that clarify?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I promised to give you an opportunity to raise the issue you wanted to raise before. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for giving me this opportunity. I shall be brief. The Defence is perhaps more than others sure that this is not a game. That is, the names which the witness mentioned was slightly different, and I think it would be useful to be very precise. I apologise if the precision was not useful. However, what I wanted to raise was the following: On the 25th, in a closed session [as interpreted], it was said by the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you're talking about what happened in closed session, I may remind you that we have -- if there's any reason to refer to anything --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said before, before this session was closed. I am saying just before what happened in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's a problem with the transcript. Because it says "the 25th, in a closed session." That's the reason I wanted to remind you. But that's a clear mistake. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will look at the transcript in English once again. Let me see what I said on the 25th. It was indicated that I had communicated to the Prosecution my satisfaction - I repeat, my satisfaction - both in French and English, with regard to certain documents. And the remark which you just said, I could not confirm that because I wasn't there. But the question is of the hearing. They heard the word "dissatisfaction" but it was dissatisfaction because in no case did I mention my satisfaction [as interpreted]. And I should like to benefit this occasion to my dissatisfaction with the fact that things were put in my mouth that I did not say. I want the things to be clear. Therefore, I express my dissatisfaction with this. And when something is said, then I want to be here. And I hope it is now clear. I do not want things put in my mouth if I am not there and which I did not say. I hope this is now clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want the Chamber to verify the issue and to come back to it, or the mere fact that I have explained what I have said now is good enough for me and it's clarified, so the issue is then closed? Of course, there always is a problem if you are absent, something might be said. And I'm only too glad to see that you went through the transcript, and at least you're in a position to follow exactly what has been said in your absence. Can I assume that this correction is what you intended, or do you want any further --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not think that this Tribunal should waste time with such things because there can be some problems of personal relations, and this has not to do with it. I think things are quite clear for everybody, but I hope that in the future, nobody will benefit from anybody's absence to put in his or her mouth words which that person has not said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reason why I asked it is that, without further investigation, of course, this Chamber is not in a position to assess whether the transcript is not correct. I can imagine "satisfaction" or "dissatisfaction" can be easily confused. This Chamber is not aware of whether this was a kind of technical problem and we might have understood it in a different way. But I do understand that you say for this moment, it's sufficient that the words, as they appear in the transcript as being the words what I supposedly had spoken are not correct, since I have spoken different words. So if that's what you intended to tell us, then it's quite clear to us. Then we could continue with your next witness, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I call Ifeta Sahic. And to assist the Trial Chamber, I indicate that she will give evidence in relation to scheduled sniping incident number 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. Mr. Usher, could you bring the witness in the courtroom. [The witness entered court] 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a witness, the rules require you to make a solemn declaration, and the text of the solemn declaration will be given to you now by the usher. Would you please make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. Miss Sahic - at least I understand that you are Miss Sahic - as a witness, you'll first be examined by the Prosecution. I do not know whether it will be Mr. Ierace who will put questions to you. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: My name is Ifeta Sahic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please come a bit closer to the microphones, or have them adjusted. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you living in August of 1993?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: At Kobilja Glava.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that in or near Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who were you living with?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: With my sister.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can hardly hear the witness. Could the microphones be adjusted, please, or the witness asked to speak up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please speak a bit louder or a bit more nearer to the microphones, Miss Sahic. The interpreters have some difficulty in hearing you. Yes, please, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In August 1993, how old were you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I was 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the 9th of -- withdraw that. On the 5th of August, 1993, at some stage during that day, did you leave your sister's place in the company of some other people?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, with these two friends of mine with whom I went to get some water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What are the names of those two friends?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Sabina Zekovic and Vildana Kapur.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You have told us that you left with them to get some water. Was there not water available where you were staying, that is, with your sister?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Well, because of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was there electricity available at your sister's place when you were living there or staying there?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Again because of the living conditions during the war. There was no water or electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How far from your sister's place was the nearest place where you could fetch water?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Thirty minutes to one hour, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before that day, had you gone to fetch water?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many people were living in the same place as you at that stage? What number of people?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot tell you the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't want to make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. When you went to fetch water with your two friends, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. did you intend to fetch water for just yourself or for other people as well?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Just myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you take anything with you to put the water in? What did you --

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you take for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Jerrycans and a cart, wheelbarrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many jerrycans, approximately?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Enough to fill the wheelbarrow, enough for us to be able to pull the wheelbarrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you gone to get water at that place before that day?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How often would you go to get water?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: When necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would that be more than once a week?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would it be more than twice a week?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Every other day or every two or three days. It really depended. When we ran out of water, we would go to collect some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you brought water back to the house, would other people use that water as well?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No. When we collected water, it was usually for the people who were living with us in that house. We all fetched water for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. When you had gone previously to collect water, was there any particular time that you would do so?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Well, we would usually go early in the morning or at dusk, when visibility is not so good. But sometimes when it was necessary, we would also go during the day, in the afternoon hours, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You say that you would usually go at times when visibility is not so good, that is, early in the morning or at dusk. Why would you do that?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Well, so that the aggressor couldn't see us. They were shooting at everyone, including civilians, everything they moved -- everything that moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who do you mean by "the aggressor"?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I specifically mean Chetniks, that is, Bosnian Serbs or, rather, the army of Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why, then, would you sometimes -- I withdraw that. You said that sometimes, when it was necessary, you would also go during the day, in the afternoon hours, for example. When would it be necessary?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: When we ran out of water, that is, when we needed water for drinking or cooking. Then it would be necessary for us to get some water, and we would go and fetch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What time was it, approximately, on the 5th of August, 1993, when you went off to collect water?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I think it was sometime between noon or in the afternoon. Maybe 10.00. I cannot remember exactly what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember why it was you went in daylight hours on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Because we didn't have any water left. So we had to collect some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were you wearing?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I was wearing my running shoes, pair of trousers, and a T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How were you wearing your hair at that stage and how long was it?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I think it was a bit shorter than it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether it was in a ponytail or loose or what?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No. I don't think I can remember that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that one of the friends who was with you was Sabina Zekovic. How was she dressed on that day when you went to collect water?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: She had a T-shirt on, also a pair of trousers, and was wearing tennis shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How old, approximately, was Sabina Zekovic at that time?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know what was her exact age, but she's a year or maybe two years older than myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You also mentioned that you went with -- I'll withdraw that. Who was the third person, the other friend who went with you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Vildana Kapur.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was she associated with your family?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: She was the sister of my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How old was she, approximately?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: She was, I believe, the same age as Sabina Zekovic. So she was a year or two older than myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was she wearing?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: She was wearing a pair of blue jeans, a black T-shirt, and sneakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In order to collect the water, did you take your trolley and jerrycans along a street?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the name of the street?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Stara Cesta, the Old Road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the name of the place where you would collect the water?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Hotonj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you make it to Hotonj?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. It was actually on our way back. We had already collected the water and we were going back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did you make it home again?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't. It happened on our way back in that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Tribunal what happened.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: On the way back home, while we were still in Stara Cesta, shooting started. We couldn't hear anything. We could only see fire, that is, bullets striking around our feet, and we could see the flash from this machine-gun, from the Death Sower, as we called it. We took shelter in an orchard which was to our left side. We lay down, but Vildana didn't want to lay down because she didn't want to get dirty so she just remained standing near a tree and got wounded. I saw that she was bleeding. She was bleeding from her left leg. And I ran down the meadow because there was a kitchen, canteen, which belonged to the police station, in the vicinity. And I called for help. And they took her to hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time the shooting started, was it coming from in front of you, to the side of you, or from behind you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: In front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mentioned that you could see the flash from this machine-gun, from the Death Sower, as you called it. Were you familiar, at that stage, as to where the confrontation lines were?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What side of the confrontation lines did you see the flash?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: The shooting came from the aggressor's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear or see anything indicating how close or where the bullets came in relation to where you were?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly where it was, but I could see it with my own eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What could you see?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I could see the aggressor's lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you seen shooting in that area before that day?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On any of those occasions, had you seen any flashes of guns, what appeared to be guns? Guns' flashes, I should say.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly. On any of those previous occasions, had you seen what appeared to be gun flashes?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, I would like to have shown to the witness Exhibit P3279C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please -- or is that the -- oh, yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise yourself in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, I refer to photograph which, in the top right-hand corner, is numbered 0215-1436.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who is the gentleman who appears to the left of you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: My father.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the photograph be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately when was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember whether it was in the last 12 months or two years?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I think it was in the last 12 months.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the street on which you are standing in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Stara Cesta.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you said earlier that was the name of the street along which you went to collect water. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I take it it's the street on which you were when the shooting started. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What can you say about the part of the road that appears in the photograph in relation to where you were when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: The very spot where I was, where you can see me standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What direction were you walking in at the time the shooting started? In other words, were you walking towards the camera or away from the camera?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Towards the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please now turn to the second of the two photographs in front of you. And on the top right-hand corner, the number 0215-1439 appears. Do you recognise anything which appears in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I recognise the photograph, but I don't think that this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you see, on the skyline towards the left of the photograph, there appears to be a tower on top of a hill?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What hill is that?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see, coming down from the tower and to the right, there appears to be a mosque, coloured white?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that particular mosque?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It's not very clear, but I think that this is the Kobilja Glava mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to indicate approximately in the photograph the area where you were when you were shot - withdraw that - when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No, not on this photograph. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown 360-degree electronically joined photograph, which is P3279A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Would you allow me a moment. Mr. President, there are two electronically joined photographs to be shown to this witness. The Exhibit Number is 3279A. I would ask the first of those be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, an image now appears on the screen that depicts a road or a street with a white-walled house to the right and a culvert to the left of the road. The road appears to be sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the street that appears -- or the road that appears in the image in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It is the street that we took on our way back, after we had collected water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you said the name of that street was Stara Cesta. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to the photograph in front of you, were you facing away from the camera or towards the camera at the time that the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Towards the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'd ask that the image be panned to the left slowly. Please stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you said that when the shooting started, you moved off the road. Do you see where you moved to, or at least which direction you moved to, from the image which is in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes; to the left, to the orchards that you can see on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, there are some large drainage-type pipes that appear in the bottom left hand of the screen, and there appears to be some low grass and some trees on an embankment to the left of the road. I'd ask that the image continue to be panned to the left. Please pause at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think the photograph in front of you now shows a number of trees on a grassy area above the culvert to the side of the road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to see where it was that you took shelter in that image?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you describe to us that position?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It can be seen on the photograph. There is a concrete pillar on the photograph, and from that pillar diagonally towards the left there is a very thin tree behind which Vildana Kapur hid, whereas we remained laying on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you tell us whereabouts in the image the concrete pillar is? In other words, is it in the centre of the picture or to the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: In the middle, ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it in a shady area or a sunny area?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: There is a shadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: A small shaded portion, and it is in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'd ask that the image be further zoomed in just above the sunny area where there appears to be a slight ridge or embankment. All right. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see what appears to be a black band around a cylindrical object on the ridge which is in shadow?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the concrete pillar I told you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. You were explaining to us whereabouts Vildana Kapur took shelter. Could you explain that position again in relation again to the concrete pillar.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: To the left in relation to the concrete pillar, where you can see this thin tree. Well, she hid behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that the thin tree which is immediately to the left and a little bit closer to the camera?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It is in the middle between two somewhat thicker trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the image be panned back so that we can see more. Please keep going. Further. Further. All right. And please continue panning to the left. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, do you see there appears to be a break in the road surface, that is, a break in the bitumen in the foreground of the image in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you still have in front of you the two photographs which you looked at earlier?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript that's P3279C.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please look at that photograph and compare it to the image on the screen. Actually, you could put the photograph right in front of you so you can look at the photograph and also look at the image on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please put it just in front of the witness so that she can properly compare it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you agree that we now have on the screen some of the area which appears in the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, I think earlier you said that at the time the shooting started, in relation to the photograph in front of you, that is the hard copy photograph which shows your father as well, you were facing towards the camera. Do you remember saying that earlier?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please now look at the image on the screen. I take it from that answer that you were also facing -- I'll withdraw that. That at the time the shooting started, you were facing towards that camera as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Piletta-Zanin is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. I was looking at the screen. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. It seems to me that the transcript -- or maybe I have misread it. "I didn't see the camera at that time" -- the way the phrase -- the question has been phrased seems to me to be somewhat enigmatic to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll be happy to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you would, please. I need some assistant -- assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please assist Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will. I will assist him. I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, please look at the image on the screen in front of you. Having regard to your evidence so far, I take it that the direction in which you were walking on the road at the time you were shot -- I withdraw that -- at the time the shooting started was in the direction coming towards the camera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It was in front of me. On the photograph, it is the location where you can see my father, and the way I'm facing here on this photograph is the direction that we took. As for the screen, it is the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, again I invite you to compare the photograph to the image on the screen. First of all, look at the photograph. Do you see that behind you to the right there is a hedge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, would you allow me to -- I see the problem you are facing. And let me just see whether I can clarify the issue. On the hard copy photo, the photo where you are together with your father, you testified that you went into the direction you were facing on the photograph. That means that you come closer to the photographer, and you are moving away from the cars behind you when the shooting started. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would mean that if we look at the screen, could perhaps this part of the -- yes. The picture on the screen looks the same to me as the picture on the hard copy photo with the difference that there are not three cars but just one car far away. Do I understand you well that, when the shooting started, you moved away from that car and moved towards where the camera is? That means approaching the person who would have taken the picture.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you now please turn the picture again to the left, turning 180 degrees. Could that be done, since we are now in the 360 degrees. Please stop. Would it also mean, Miss Sahic, that if you look now on the screen, not on the photo any more, that when the shooting started, you were moving away from the house which is now on the right-hand side and just in front of you? So moving to the trees further on to the hills in the further distance?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did this assist you, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. President. Perhaps we could return to the image on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have to apologise because I've forgotten about the break, and since the tape is almost empty. We'll resume at 1.00 since we are late now. We adjourn until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Miss Sahic, you still can hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please come as close to the microphones as possible. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might the image be restored to the screen. That's the photographic image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us earlier that you could see the flash from the gun at the time that the shooting started. Can you see in that image in front of you now where that flash was?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, the image shows the road with a culvert to the left, and then a slope on the right that is sloping down from the road. Can you describe, having regard to the image, where you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. saw the flash?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It was on the road in front of these cracks, in front of that crack there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the operator zoom the photograph in -- withdraw that. Just stop for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say a "crack," do you mean a crack on the road surface?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you talking about where you were at the time that you saw the flash?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to ask you if you can see somewhere in that photograph in front of you at the moment where you saw the actual flash of the gun itself. Not where you were standing when you saw it, but rather where you saw the flash to be.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It was a flash from the bullet that hit the asphalt, the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Did you hear any gunfire sounds at the time of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It was all split-second timing. It all happened out of the blue, suddenly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that you were positioned approximately where the break in the road surface appears, and I think you described it as a crack. And from your earlier evidence, it would seem -- I'll stop at that point. Is that the case, you were standing where there was a break in the road surface when you heard the shooting?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And you were facing up the road as it appears in the image in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do apologise, but I'd like us to be more specific. Are we speaking about the three-dimensional photograph or the other photograph? Because I saw that there were cracks on both in apparently different positions. So could I ask Mr. Ierace's assistance with more specifics in that regard? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. As a matter of fact, in the testimony before, there are two cracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the image be restored to the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Looking at the image on the screen in front of you -- I'll withdraw that. When the shooting occurred, I think you said earlier that it came from in front of you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It would follow from your earlier evidence that the area in front of you was towards the ridge or hill which appears at the end of the road. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether, based on what you saw and heard, that was the area from which the shooting appeared to originate?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In this electronic photograph which you were shown before the break, from time to time we have seen some pipes lying in the culvert. Do you recall seeing those pipes?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: They weren't there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: The photographs were taken quite awhile afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, I would like the witness and the rest of the Trial Chamber to see a second 360-degree photograph. Might that be shown now? It's the same exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The same exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but a different 360-degree photograph. Could it be shown on the screen? Yes. Yes. Perhaps I'm a bit impatient. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think for the benefit of the transcript, we now see a grassy slope with some trees, and to the bottom of the slope, to the right of the image, there appears to be a road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what appears in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: This photograph isn't quite clear to me. I suppose it's from the angle that the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the photograph be panned slowly to the left. Please keep panning to the left. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, I think we have just seen 360 degrees from the camera position. Do you recognise that area?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: That's the road which we call Stara Cesta, or Old Road, and the meadow with the orchard, with the fruit trees, where it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As the photograph moved around, did you notice where you took cover?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you also notice where Vildana Kapur took cover?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We'll go around once more, and could you please tell us when to stop as you see either of those two positions, where you took cover and where Vildana Kapur took cover. Do you understand? Do you understand what I would like you to do?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please move the image to the left.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: On the meadow there, next to the pillar. The picture's not quite clear, but there's the thin tree that I pointed out to you earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Pause the image there. Now, for the benefit of the transcript, again we see a green lawn area with tree shadows on it and, beyond that, a ridge running across the image, which is in shadow. We see in silhouette a trunk which is split fairly close to the ground, and beyond it, in shadow, what appears to be a pillar with a black horizontal band.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've referred to the tree which is in front of the pillar. Who took shelter there?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: To the left of the pillar, slightly to the left. That's the tree where Vildana Kapur was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to move the image to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And please indicate when you see the position where you took cover.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: It's precisely that tree there, the one on the left, to the left of the pillar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think in the image we can see at the moment, there is the sun, which appears as a white area in the sky. Could you describe the tree in relation to the position of the sun.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Underneath, just below it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean slightly to the left or slightly to the right?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Slightly to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Who took shelter there?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Vildana Kapur.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And who took shelter at the other position that you pointed out?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Sabina Zekovic, on the grassy patch where we lay down, and I did, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that you took shelter at the same place as Sabina Zekovic?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Near the tree. I can't tell you the exact spot now. But near this tree, we lay down, the two of us. We lay down on the grass.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I don't require to see the image any more at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you told us that Vildana Kapur you think was a few years older than you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not she was working or studying or doing anything else at that stage?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that you saw blood on her left leg during or after the shooting. Did she say anything as to whether or not she had been injured during that episode?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did she say?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: That she had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice whether she appeared to have any difficulty in moving after she said that?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Tell us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: She couldn't move. She was holding her leg with her hands, and she was screaming out that she was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What leg was she holding, which one?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Her left leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice the presence of any blood?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: On her jeans, I saw blood streaming down her leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which leg?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Her left leg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I see in the transcript a couple of lines before that the witness testified that you've told us that you saw blood on her left leg during or after the shooting. So it seems a bit repetitious.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At any stage -- withdraw that. At the time the shooting started, was there anyone else around that you saw, apart from your two friends?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice around that time whether there were any military -- withdraw that. Did you see any military vehicles or other military equipment in the vicinity at the time of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At around that time, had you heard any shooting or other firing of weaponry appearing to come from the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I heard some shooting, but not that day. I heard that there had been shooting, but not that day, and that's why we decided to go and fetch water that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your last answer, had you heard any shooting at any stage earlier that day, that is, before the shooting when Vildana Kapur was hit?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Well, there was gunfire all the time, every day. One couldn't really say when it would start, at what time, or where. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you earlier said, "I heard some shooting but not that day," did you mean - pardon me - did you mean by that you had not heard shooting that day coming from the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You've told us that there was gunfire all the time every day.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that apply to the -- to where you were living? In other words, you could hear that from where you were living?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you ever heard gunfire apparently the result of weapons being fired from anywhere in the vicinity of where Vildana was shot?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How long before Vildana was shot did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Was it the same day that Vildana was shot?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That completes the examination-in-chief, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Is the Defence ready for cross-examining the witness? Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you very much. With the permission of your Chamber, I will cross-examine this witness, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the interpreters are having difficulty hearing you. If you could please move the microphone closer to you or speak up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, it only means getting -- putting the microphone higher up, and I shall be very happy to do it. And is it now better for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sahic, the Defence will now put questions to you. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To begin with, good afternoon, Witness, and thank you for coming here. You several times answers [as interpreted], and these are pages 57, line 99 [as interpreted], you answered a question that was asked you by the Prosecution whether it was these -- the -- who was firing, and you said it was aggressors and then you said it was Chetniks. Now, my question is as follows: Could you tell this Chamber what is exactly a Chetnik?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: A Chetnik is a person who killed civilians or anything that moved on the surface. A Chetnik and -- I do not draw a mark of equality between a Chetnik and a Serb. Serbs are people like everybody else, who respect and observe their faith, and Chetniks are those who killed, who even killed civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And therefore, if I am following you, to your mind a Chetnik is a man who kills without distinction, without discrimination.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What person?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. For you, therefore, madam, according to your definition, a Chetnik is a person who kills indiscriminately.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I deduce this, and that -- hence my question. Could one say then that there were some Chetniks in the Bosnia -- in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which we call Bosniak here, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I go back a few questions, Mr. Piletta-Zanin said that earlier the witness had said the firing came from the aggressors, "and then you said it was Chetniks." At that stage, Mr. Piletta-Zanin did not add the third description which the witness gave earlier on. I did not object at that time, having regard to the rest of the question, but now it becomes relevant. And if one goes back to the page at line reference that he gave, one will see that third category.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that would be exactly line -- page -- I think it was -- could you assist me in the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking the assistance of both of you since you both seem to know what page it was and I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's page 57, line 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sixty-seven?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Fifty-seven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fifty-seven. Let me just find it. Fifty-seven, and you said line --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Twenty-one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please, when you refer to the earlier statement, you've got it in front of you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, quote then since there is some objection, more in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be happy to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. As I was saying, page 57, line 21. And perhaps it could be of interest. Yes. The question that was asked of you was: When you spoke about the aggressors --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to quote the text, Mr. President, now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're referring to the answer earlier given, and the Prosecution objects since you're quoting only part of it, and now you're asking whether there were any Chetniks in the Bosnia-Herzegovinan army, and as far as I understand, the objection is that the witness earlier indicated in what army she situated the Chetniks quite precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Mr. President, the objection, if I understood Mr. Ierace, and that is one of numerous objections that we heard today, had to do that I was referring imprecisely to an answer, and the witness answered the question and said that it was Chetniks or Serbs and so on and so forth. What I said, having heard the witness's answer to my question, and that was: "A Chetnik is a person who kills indiscriminately." Now I'm now asking my question, a second question, in relation to what was said, and I do not see that this objection can stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the objection stands, and I'll explain to you why, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. In the answer to the question of the Prosecution, I think the witness gave a -- specified more in detail what a Chetnik was as far as the ethnicity is concerned, and also she situates Chetniks in a specific army. You later asked her to explain what she exactly meant by that, and then I think she gave a further explanation not in contradiction what she said before, but she explained that she would make a distinction between other Serbians and Chetniks by the indiscriminate shooting or killing. So that was a further precision, but she did not take any distance from the definition given at that time. I do understand it's only a limited reference to what at that time she said Chetniks were. But you're now asking her whether they were in another army than she situated them. Apart from the relevance, you first then should ask her whether this earlier answer was correct or not. But please proceed, and keep in mind what I said about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will then move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir -- Witness, can we take it as a principal -- if I understood you well -- that the aggressors are always Chetniks. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my other questions will be referring to this electronic image. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we then, please, show it on the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Piletta-Zanin could indicate whether he wishes the first or the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on the road or in the orchard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I understand Mr. Ierace well, there are two electronic images with the same reference. So perhaps Mr. Ierace could give me the reference. We have two of them, and I really do not know. I must admit that I am lost, and I really do not know now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, there's one document number attached to this photograph. And I'd just like to know, since I assume that you know what you're questioning about, that you want the road or the orchard?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both, both, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which one first?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The road. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see this road?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we're still waiting for it to be shown on the screen, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have now the orchard on the screen. So could we please have the -- it's a bit impractical, Mr. Ierace, to have two different 360 degrees photographs in the same number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can tell you that this is the only incident where there are two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm only too glad to hear so. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as soon as the other picture is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I have problem with the screen because, on my screen, I can't see anything. Is that normal? Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It does take some time to cue up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You should see it on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now want to be clear. Is that the road or what? I really need Mr. Ierace's assistance. Is that the road?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have anything on your screen at this moment, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? A picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because what I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the screen. As far as I can see now, and I can see some seven screens, that there has always been a road on the screen with a small part of a white building with a small part of a red roof on the outer right-hand side of the picture. Is that what you have got in front of you? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is exactly it. And I thank you. The question that I wanted to ask with regard to this type of photograph is would it be possible to make it so that the camera takes also the elevation, that is, not to move only horizontally, to the left Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. horizontal, but to zoom it and to raise it up. I don't know whether it is technically possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could just ask. Could it be zoomed in the picture as we have it now. Yes. And would you please indicate, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whether we are in the right position or you should like to be a bit to the left or a bit to the right and whether you want to go upwards or downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perfect, perfect, Mr. President. And now, can we also do, and I'm asking the witness, a 360 degrees, but keeping this elevation? I think it wasn't used before, but I would like to have it this way, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 360 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could that be slowly. Perhaps, yes, that's the direction we had before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Can we go a little bit back. I'm sorry, but can we slowly move to the right now. A little bit more. Can we -- there now. Thank you. Can you now zoom it in the direction of the elevation of that hill that we see on the horizon, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we are asking for zoom. Yes. You want it further? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a little bit more, please. And a little bit more. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So the question is as follows: Can you identify this ridge which we see in the upper part of the photograph before you? And I'm saying for the transcript that we see here a kind of a rocky ridge with a dome about it which is not very visible but which looks like a barren outcrop.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the place exactly. And below that, beneath that rock, one can see something white. But that is just a cluster of houses from which the shot came.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question is, or was, as follows: With a reference to this elevation which I just mentioned, could you please give us the name of that place, of that elevation?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So what is it called?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: That place beneath that dome, beneath this outcrop, is called Poljine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need to ask that question again. I thought I had asked it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, I wasn't asking you what was beneath or above but the name of that elevation which you see on the screen. If you don't know it, say you don't know. But just a moment ago, I think I heard you say yes.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is called Poljine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So the name of this hill is Poljine. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when I look at the clock, I see that it's a quarter to 2.00. Would there be a suitable moment shortly to interrupt the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Defence also wishes to comply with the time, and we shall then resume our examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Sahic, for all kind of practical reasons, we have to stop for today. This will mean that we resume tomorrow morning at 9.00, and then the examination will continue. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you're still standing. Was there any practical problem or is it just... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. I was simply absentminded. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
